layoutContracts: 3-row chrome intent: Row 1 omnibox + Save/Alerts CTAs; Row 2 primary filter chips; Row 3 results count + filter summary + sort
Degraded search honesty: SSR/client timeout or fetch failure must not present as true zero inventory without a retry/degraded affordance
Count/sort row: dedicated visible stamp in split (N homes · scope/filters · sorted by…). 390 list names the list (N homes). in this map view only when the map is on screen.
390 filters are one All filters control. Chip set is sm+ so pills do not clip.
Search-as-you-move: pan/zoom re-queries the visible area; list + markers stay in lockstep from ONE viewport fetch
Split body: map + results side-by-side on desktop; intentional mobile list/map toggle (not dual conflicting chrome)
V3Chrome is sticky in flow, not fixed. Search-app-frame height is calc(100dvh - 3.5rem) with margin-top 0. Filter dock sticks at top 3.5rem.

SITE-44 basemap: every public Google map paints lib/maps/v3-basemap.ts — a navy-on-cream style array matched to V3Atlas's ladder (highway navy 34%, arterial 22%, local 10%, water 12%, boundary 55%, labels 70%). No mapId is ever passed: a Map ID makes Google discard the style array and serve a Cloud Console style this repo cannot read, which is how the search map came to be stock Google tiles. Google's own controls are off in one place (V3_MAP_CHROME_OFF); the wordmark and terms links stay, by the Maps terms of service.

SITE-44 marks: clustering never stops (V3_CLUSTER_MAX_ZOOM) and merges anything closer than one mark's width (V3_CLUSTER_RADIUS_PX, with supercluster's extent pinned to the 256px tile so the radius means screen pixels). The opening fitBounds clears a mark and a half on every edge (v3FitPadding) and frames the boundary AND the pins, not the boundary alone. A mark that would still cross an edge slides in, and its caret slides the opposite way so it keeps pointing at its own house. A cluster badge's diameter is its count, and hovering it names the count and the ask range it holds.

SITE-44 claim: the results rail opens on a sentence, not a count — how many homes the frame draws, the ask range across them, the place, and a collapsed section 0 trace. It is derived from the same array the cards and the pins render, through publishWholePropertyAmount, so a lease rate and a fractional share never enter the range. The mobile peek carries the same claim beside the filter-match count, and each half names its own population.

SITE-44 card mark: every result card carries a price-per-square-foot position against the homes currently in view — a track for the full spread, a band for the middle half, a dot for this home (components/search/ppsf-band.ts). A home with no living area renders the mark's empty state rather than dropping it.

SITE-44 filter weights: Price and Beds/Baths are the row's heavy controls (srch-chip--key, 700); every other pill and the Save-search control sit at the row's base 500, and the two actions sit behind a hairline.
sectionOrder: APP FRAME, not a document. It renders no breadcrumb and no footer on purpose: the map/list split is viewport-fit.
ResultsStamp -- the count and the stamp
SearchAlertCapture -- save this search, mounted with the query surface so the ask travels with the filters
HideAwareSearchMap / MapSearchView -- search-as-you-move; pan/zoom re-queries the visible area
SearchResults -- the list, in lockstep with the markers from ONE viewport fetch

shotSpec.capture: first viewport, scripts/take-route-shots.mjs, scale 1, palette-quantized, http://127.0.0.1:3172/homes-for-sale?city=Bend on wt/site-72-20260910

tasteReview.beats: Redfin Bend map search (https://www.redfin.com/city/16163/OR/Bend): this fold wins on reaching a broker (541.703.3095, Save this search) and citing Oregon Data Share; it loses map-as-product — Redfin encodes price on pins, this encodes headcount on Google-signed cream tiles. Also loses brand cartography to V3Atlas on /cities/bend, which does not still wear a Google wordmark.

defects.finding: Desktop still shows the Google wordmark, Map data ©2026 Google, and Google road geometry under cream tint. Clusters encode headcount, not ask. A buyer cannot read affordability from the field. This is a skin on Google, not house Atlas.
The left half of the 1440 fold is a portal photo–price–spec stack. The $/sqft mark is labeled but still quiet, so the rail reads as inventory chrome rather than a drawing.
The Bend field is a static bordered input with a mic in the default shot. Live focus morphs into the command list, but the first-viewport capture does not show that interaction.
PRICE / Any price is a tall tick track with dual thumbs. Evaluator still wanted the beui navy-fill bounce bar; house motion keeps ease-out without bounce.
The strongest number on 375 can still be a cluster headcount; the hero claim overlay names the same population as the peek.
SAVED AREAS, Map/List/SORT, and the inventory line stack onto the map and clip the south of the field.
Desktop and mobile aspect ratios frame different pin sets, so ask maxima can differ across the shot pair even when each claim is honest to its viewport.

tasteReview.verdict: Better than a 32: navy clusters, a sourced 500, listing cards with price/address/beds/baths/sqft, a labeled $/sqft-vs-map mark, a tick-stop price row, morph-on-focus place search, and a mobile hero claim replace a naked Google embed. Still loses to Redfin on price-encoded pins and to V3Atlas on unsigned cartography; beui-morphing-search and house-atlas remain named defects for the next pass.
